one_month_reasoning: No company-scheduled event falls inside 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-29. Q1 FY26 was reported Nov 20, 2025 and Q1 FY27 is expected in late November or around Dec 1, 2026, both outside the window (supervisor confirmed). Investor Day (Sep 17) already reaffirmed Q1 and FY27 guidance. Minor in-window items: Xero's US price change from Oct 1, QuickBooks renewals continuing at the new Aug 1 list prices (Plus $140, Advanced $340, confirmed on Intuit's own product-update page), and news about AI tax and bookkeeping agents. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways: momentum is negative after a ~23% one-month fall, but the stock sits near its 52-week low, where reversals are common. I stay close to a symmetric lognormal centred on $268 with ~14% monthly vol (50%/3.5), with a very slight downward tilt for momentum. This is essentially unchanged from round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of FY28E SBC-inclusive EPS $25.5 x 12.5x = $319 (60%) and a normalized SBC-burdened FCF yield leg: FY26 FCF of $5.34B after removing the one-off $1.28B OBBBA deferred-tax add-back, grown 10%/yr to $6.46B in FY28, at an 8.5% required yield, less $0.5B net debt, over 255M shares = $296 (40%). Blended about $310 (round 1: $336).

bear.story: In the 2027 tax season TurboTax loses share again (units down against a growing self-prepared e-file category, with FreeTaxUSA, Credit Karma free filing and AI agents such as Perplexity and TaxGPT taking share). The QuickBooks price step-ups (Plus +22%, Advanced +24% on Aug 1) push online customer growth from 3% toward flat. The FY28 guide implies high-single-digit growth at best. The multiple compresses toward ~7.5-8x on ~$22-23 EPS, between the HRB-like 6.6x floor and today's multiple.

base.story: FY27 comes in roughly at guide (~$23 EPS). TurboTax units are flat-ish while Live/assisted grows. QBO pricing sticks with modest churn, and heavy buybacks shrink the share count ~4% net a year. The AI-disruption discount persists, and the stock trades at ~11.5x FY28 EPS of ~$25.5.

bull.story: The tax season proves resilient: agents integrate with TurboTax rather than replace it, and Direct File stays suspended. Intuit Enterprise Suite and mid-market scale, customer growth re-accelerates from 3%, and the multiple recovers to ~16-17x FY28 EPS.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$190 the stock would sit near 8.3x guided FY27 SBC-inclusive EPS and ~11% normalized SBC-burdened FCF yield. That level only makes sense if the market is pricing an actual earnings decline (lost TurboTax units in the 2027 season, QuickBooks churn after the price step-ups, or a guide cut), not just sentiment. I keep $190 rather than the supervisor's $195: the H&R Block ~6.6x comparable shows that de-rated tax businesses can trade lower without a fundamental break, so a slightly lower bar avoids calling ordinary de-rating a break.

reasoning: Round-2 revisions follow the supervisor's evidence-backed findings. (1) FY26 OCF of $8.84B includes a one-off $1.28B OBBBA deferred-tax add-back (cash taxes $281M vs $1.4B in FY25). Normalized SBC-burdened FCF is ~$5.3B, not $6.6B, so my FCF leg falls from $357 to $296 at an unchanged 8.5% required yield. (2) Shares outstanding are 267.2M, not 277M, so the market cap is ~$71.6B and the current normalized FCF yield is ~7.5%. (3) H&R Block trades at ~6.6x forward, a lower ex-growth floor, so I fatten the left tail and set the bear case at $175 (was $180) with 27% weight. (4) TurboTax units -2% against IRS self-prepared e-file +1.7% is primary evidence of share loss. It replaces my forum and app-ranking snippets, which I now drop as number drivers. I also trim FY28 EPS to $25.5 because FY27 margin leverage came partly from the one-off restructuring, so the P/E leg is $319. The blended fair value is ~$310 (was $336). New alternative-lane checks: Intuit's own product-update page confirms the Aug 1 QBO list prices (Plus $115 to $140, +22%; Advanced $275 to $340, +24%). The '13-70%' figures from migration-vendor blogs compare against older or promotional prices and are discounted, as the supervisor asked. Intuit's disclosures show online paying customers +3% (2 points slower), a harder datapoint on QuickBooks volume than the blogs. I found no Reddit or ProAdvisor data showing a migration wave. I keep the 12-month median at ~$285, below fair value, because the disruption discount is unlikely to clear before the 2027 tax-season data and momentum is negative. Distribution: roughly lognormal around $285 with sigma ~0.46, left tail slightly fattened for the HRB floor and right tail trimmed for the lower corrected fair value (P>=536 from 0.085 to 0.07). It is consistent with scenarios of $175/$295/$420 at 27/50/23 (mean ~$291). Research this round was limited to 3 searches.
